title: What doesn't concern you
hook: part of a person's good Islam is leaving what doesn't concern him
tomorrow: what do you wish for the person standing next to you?

segments.voice: Yesterday: leave what makes you doubt, and take the clear thing beside it; but a vague worry doesn't cancel certainty. Leave the doubt. Today, something else to leave.

The group chat hasn't stopped buzzing since lunch. Screenshots, theories, voice notes: somebody's breakup, taken apart by people who barely know either of them. You haven't typed a word, and you've still spent an hour inside it. Yesterday's question asked what you could quit today that makes your faith better. Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, naming exactly that. Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what doesn't concern them.
screen: `SCREENSHOTS, THEORIES, VOICE NOTES.` → `AN HOUR, WITHOUT A WORD.` → `LEAVE WHAT DOESN'T CONCERN YOU.`

segments.voice: Look at the shape of it. Hadith after hadith this week asked you to do something: intend, pray, keep, guard. This one improves a person's faith by subtraction. The leaving is the good deed. So what doesn't concern you? Commentators describe it as what you don't need, for your religion or your life: idle talk, other people's private affairs, curiosity that feeds nothing but itself. Which can be a good part of a scrolling day. But careful. This isn't permission to stop caring. Hadith seven said religion is nasihah, sincere goodwill, even toward ordinary people. Helping someone, warning them kindly, stopping harm: all of that concerns you. What you leave is the prying, the guessing, the piling on. So the real skill is one question, asked in the moment: is this mine to carry, or only mine to watch? In al-Tirmidhi's collection, the line is short enough to fit inside that moment. One to tell a friend tonight: here, quitting something is counted as a sign of good faith.
screen: `GOOD FAITH BY SUBTRACTION.` · `IDLE TALK, PRIVATE AFFAIRS.` · `GOODWILL STILL CONCERNS YOU.` · `MINE TO CARRY, OR TO WATCH?` · then, large: `NOT MY CONCERN.`

segments.voice: Put your phone face down and rest a hand on it, then close your eyes. Let one matter come to mind that you've been following and that isn't really yours: a feud, a rumor, someone else's business. Picture setting it down on the table beside you, and leave it there for the rest of the sit.
screen: `PHONE FACE DOWN.` · `ONE MATTER THAT ISN'T YOURS.` · `SET IT DOWN.`

segments.voice: What doesn't concern you: the talk, the prying and the curiosity you don't need. Leaving it is part of the excellence of a person's Islam.
Here's the line: not my concern, said kindly, and the hour it hands back to you. Fourteen days, complete.

screen: `DAY 1440 COUNTS.` → `YEAR FIVE · 14 OF 365.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DO YOU WISH FOR THE PERSON STANDING NEXT TO YOU?`

howItsDone: Muslim teachers quote this hadith against gossip, prying and idle talk, and pair it with the duty of goodwill: helping, advising kindly and stopping harm are not counted as 'what doesn't concern you'.

match.prompt: what to leave, what to keep — tap the pairs.

myth: this hadith means never getting involved in other people's problems
helping, kind advice and stopping harm concern you. it's idle prying and piling on that you leave.
the hadith counts leaving something as part of the excellence of a person's Islam
part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what doesn't concern them.

fork.setup: through the wall, your neighbors are shouting again, and tonight it sounds like someone could be hurt. 'not my concern'?
options: if someone may be in danger, it concerns you: call emergency help.
it's their private business, and leaving it is part of good Islam.
listen closely first, so you know the whole story before anything.
fork.reveal: leaving what doesn't concern you never means leaving someone in danger. harm and help are your concern; call local emergency help (911 in the US).

original.script: مِنْ حُسْنِ إِسْلَامِ الْمَرْءِ تَرْكُهُ مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ
original.say: min HUS-ni is-LAA-mil MAR' tar-KU-hu maa laa ya'-NEE-hi
original.note: Arabic: part of the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.

trapdoor: what you thought: mind your own business.
what it means: part of the excellence of someone's Islam is leaving the talk and prying that isn't theirs to carry.
what a scholar hears: husn al-islam, the excellence of a person's Islam, and the line between what concerns you, like goodwill and stopping harm, and idle curiosity.
guess: stepping back from matters that aren't yours
staying silent when someone is in trouble
avoiding people from outside your community

chat.says: midterms done 🙏 but a classmate's breakup is all over the group chat. everyone wants my take. jump in?
options: Step out; it's not yours. If she needs a friend, talk to her privately.
Jump in, so at least someone fair is telling the story right.
Stay in and read it all, but just don't post anything yourself.
chat.meaning: Leaving what doesn't concern you is part of good Islam. Prying is left; goodwill, like a private word to a friend, still concerns you.

Abu Hurayrah.meaning: a companion of the Prophet who reported this hadith

al-Tirmidhi.meaning: a scholar whose hadith collection includes this report

nasihah.meaning: sincere goodwill; counsel given for someone's good

sources.ref: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 2317; Sunan Ibn Majah 3976 (Abu Hurayrah: part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him)
